# Temple Scroll Column 42 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 42 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 42:8 — "do for him according to the whole statute" vs. "perform the complete statute" vs. "full purification procedure" — phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they shall do for him according to the whole statute of purification" | Literal Hebrew syntax |
| LOGOS | "they shall perform for him the complete statute of purification" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the full purification procedure must be carried out for him" | Modern restructured |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's phrasing for its closer adherence to Hebrew word order.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 42:10 — "his uncleanness is still upon him" vs. "his impurity persists" vs. "his uncleanness stays on him" — persistence idiom

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his uncleanness is still upon him" | Literal — tumato bo od |
| LOGOS | "his impurity persists upon him" | Formal compressed |
| PNEUMA | "his uncleanness stays on him" | Colloquial simplification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "his uncleanness is still upon him." Preserves the Hebrew idiom faithfully.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 42:14 — "sons of Israel" vs. "children of Israel" vs. "people of Israel" — bene Yisrael

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sons of Israel" | Literal bene |
| LOGOS | "the children of Israel" | Inclusive formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the people of Israel" | Dynamic modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sons of Israel" per EMET. The literal rendering is consistent with project convention for bene Yisrael.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 42:15 — "sanctify" vs. "consecrate" vs. "set apart" — qiddesh rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sanctify" | Traditional rendering of qiddesh |
| LOGOS | "consecrate" | Formal liturgical synonym |
| PNEUMA | "set apart" | Dynamic meaning-based rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sanctify" per EMET. Consistent with project terminology throughout.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 42:16 — "detestable" vs. "abominable" vs. "repulsive" — shiqqutz rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "detestable" | Standard rendering for shiqqutz |
| LOGOS | "abominable" | Formal elevated term |
| PNEUMA | "repulsive" | Visceral modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "detestable" per EMET. Consistent with established project rendering of shiqqutz-root terms.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 42:16 — "dwells in your midst" vs. "dwells in your midst" vs. "lives among you" — divine indwelling

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "who dwells in your midst" | Literal shokhen be-tokh |
| LOGOS | "who dwells in your midst" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "who lives among you" | Simplified modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "who dwells in your midst" per EMET and LOGOS. "Dwells" preserves the technical theological language of divine indwelling (shekhinah).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
